_about: Mercy and restoration side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of mercy and of restoring that more than one book shares, from Exodus and the psalms to the prophets, the Gospels and the letters, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.alike: The LORD is called "compassionate and gracious" (Exodus 34:6, Psalm 86:15, Psalm 103:8) or "gracious and compassionate" (Nehemiah 9:17, Nehemiah 9:31, Psalm 111:4, Psalm 145:8, Joel 2:13, Jonah 4:2), "slow to anger" (Exodus 34:6, Numbers 14:18, Nehemiah 9:17, Psalm 86:15, Psalm 103:8, Psalm 145:8, Joel 2:13, Jonah 4:2, Nahum 1:3) and "abounding in loving devotion" (Exodus 34:6, Numbers 14:18, Psalm 86:15, Psalm 103:8, Psalm 145:8, Joel 2:13, Jonah 4:2); James 5:11 has "full of compassion and mercy", as Psalm 116:5 has "full of compassion".
rows.different: Exodus 34:6 is the LORD calling it out as He passes in front of Moses; Nehemiah and the Psalms say it to Him or of Him, and in Jonah 4:2 it follows his "This is why I was so quick to flee toward Tarshish." Exodus 34:7, Numbers 14:18 and Nahum 1:3 go on "will by no means leave the guilty unpunished", Joel 2:13 and Jonah 4:2 go on to relenting "from sending disaster", Micah 7:18 asks "Who is a God like You" of Him "who pardons iniquity", and Proverbs and James 1:19 use "slow to anger" of people.

rows.alike: "Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His loving devotion endures forever" is said or sung in Chronicles, the Psalms and Jeremiah, and Psalm 136 makes "His loving devotion endures forever" the second half of every one of its twenty-six verses.
rows.different: In Chronicles and Ezra it is given by "Heman, Jeduthun, and the rest of those chosen" (1 Chronicles 16:41), by the trumpeters and singers as "the temple, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud" (2 Chronicles 5:13), by all the Israelites when they saw "the fire coming down" (2 Chronicles 7:3), by those "singing" before the army (2 Chronicles 20:21), and by "all the people" "because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid" (Ezra 3:11), where it is "His loving devotion to Israel"; in Psalm 118:2-4 "Israel", "the house of Aaron" and "those who fear the LORD" are each called to say it, and Psalm 138:8 says "Your loving devotion" to the LORD directly; in Jeremiah 33:11 the same words are what "those bringing thank offerings into the house of the LORD" are heard "saying", and the verse goes on "For I will restore the land from captivity as in former times, says the LORD."

rows.alike: God's "great compassion" or "great mercy" is named: "His mercies are great" (2 Samuel 24:14), "in Your great compassion" three times in Nehemiah 9, "Great are Your mercies, O LORD" (Psalm 119:156), "because of Your great compassion" (Daniel 9:18), "By His great mercy" (1 Peter 1:3).
rows.different: David says it choosing "the hand of the LORD" over "the hands of men", and Daniel 9:18 sets it against "our righteous acts", as Titus 3:5 sets "according to His mercy" against "the righteous deeds we had done"; Isaiah 54:7 has "with great compassion I will bring you back" to a "you" the verse does not name, Jeremiah 31:20 has "I have great compassion for him" of Ephraim, Luke 1:58 has "her neighbors and relatives" rejoicing that "the Lord had shown her great mercy", and 1 Peter 1:3 and Titus 3:5 both join mercy to "new birth".

rows.alike: Mercy is asked of people beside justice: "to act justly, to love mercy" (Micah 6:8), "Administer true justice. Show loving devotion and compassion" (Zechariah 7:9), "justice, mercy, and faithfulness" (Matthew 23:23); and mercy shown is set beside mercy received: "Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy" (Matthew 5:7), "judgment without mercy will be shown to anyone who has not been merciful" (James 2:13).
rows.different: Micah 6:8 and Zechariah 7:9 give it as what the LORD requires and says, and Hosea 12:6 joins it to "return to your God"; Matthew 23:23 has "Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites!" before "justice, mercy, and faithfulness", Luke 6:36 measures it by "your Father", Matthew 18:33 asks "Shouldn't you have had mercy on your fellow servant, just as I had on you?", and James 2:13 ends "Mercy triumphs over judgment."
